architecture.before: SVG + CSS gradients/animations + Web Animations API; no Three.js/WebGL renderer in the active Galaxy background
architecture.after: Existing SVG/CSS/Web Animations architecture preserved and augmented with a lightweight adaptive Canvas 2D depth-star layer
architecture.principle: Evolve the existing visual concept instead of replacing it

visual: Broad nebula shapes relied on large Gaussian blur values and could read as soft haze instead of structured cosmic depth
Depth came mostly from separate SVG objects and a small set of DOM stars
Hero composition did not explicitly reserve a calm readability zone behind headline and CTAs
Mobile fallback was functional but visually simpler than the desktop identity
technical: Existing full/balanced/static capability tiers already protected weak devices and reduced-motion users

visual_improvements: Added three independent star-depth planes with distinct scale, brightness, parallax and drift characteristics
Moved the landing's richest galactic composition toward the product demo/right side while reducing visual competition behind the hero copy
Added a dedicated readability field behind headline/CTA regions without placing overlays above interactive content
Rebuilt nebula SVG structure with broad atmospheric layers plus narrower luminous cores and sparse crisp dust points
Sharpened main and distant spiral galaxies with smaller blur kernels and secondary fine arm strokes
Reduced planet prominence so the scene reads more like deep space and less like a crowded solar-system illustration
Kept movement slow and atmospheric rather than screensaver-like
technical_improvements: Added GalaxyDepthCanvas.tsx using Canvas 2D rather than introducing a new 3D dependency
Capped devicePixelRatio per tier/quality to improve sharpness without unbounded GPU/memory cost
Added deterministic seeded star generation to avoid visual layout jitter between repaints
Used requestAnimationFrame with capped paint frequency instead of rendering at display refresh rate
Used window.scrollY inside the existing paint loop for depth response, avoiding a new scroll listener
Pointer parallax activates only on capable full-tier devices with a fine pointer
Canvas loop stops when the document is hidden or animation is disabled
Existing comet, scene-plan and tier systems remain intact

desktop_vs_mobile.full_desktop: Rich three-plane canvas field, capped high-DPR rendering, subtle pointer/scroll parallax, full SVG scene and slow atmospheric drift
desktop_vs_mobile.balanced: Lower canvas opacity/density/DPR and 24fps paint budget; existing scene planner keeps fewer assets
desktop_vs_mobile.mobile_static: No canvas animation; premium CSS-only star/nebula fallback with the same Galaxy identity and a simplified composition
desktop_vs_mobile.reduced_motion: No animated galaxy drift; static fallback remains visually complete

notes: No extra scroll listener for the starfield
Existing hardware/save-data/reduced-motion tiers continue to decide scene complexity

tunable_parameters.ambient_drift: DEPTH_DRIFT and premium CSS animation durations
tunable_parameters.nebula_intensity: landing nebula opacity/filter declarations in space-galaxy-premium.css
